name: Paternoster Aglianico del Vulture Don Anselmo 2010
text:
## Paternoster Aglianico del Vulture Don Anselmo 2010

**The story.** Paternoster is one of the most important wineries of [Basilicata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilicata), the little-known region in Italy's instep, and has been producing and bottling [Aglianico del Vulture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aglianico_del_Vulture) since 1925. It stands on the slopes of [Monte Vulture](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Monte+Vulture,+Basilicata,+Italy&t=k), an extinct volcano, so it makes, as its US importer says, "a volcanic wine in the literal sense of the term" ([Vintus](https://vintus.com/?p=31844)).

**The wine: Don Anselmo.** Don Anselmo is the estate's landmark wine: 100% [Aglianico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aglianico), Basilicata's native grape, dedicated to the founder, Anselmo Paternoster, and to the family's roots in the Vulture ([Vintus](https://vintus.com/?p=31844)). Jancis Robinson's Walter Scott "long admired the Paternoster estate", scoring later vintages of Don Anselmo 17.5 and 17++ out of 20.

**The vintage.** Jancis Robinson's vintage charts don't cover Basilicata.

**What the critics say for 2010.**
- I couldn't read a published critic's note for the 2010 Don Anselmo on pages I could open, so I've left critics out rather than guess.
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 89.7** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is sixteen years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2016 to 2031. It should be mature now, with dark cherry, tar, smoke and earth. Decant one to two hours ahead and serve at 17°C.

**Food.** Southern Italian food: lamb with peppers, slow-cooked ragù, grilled sausages with fennel, or aged pecorino and caciocavallo.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the stores on this site lists Paternoster at the moment.

**Curious details**
- **A volcano's wine.** Monte Vulture is an extinct volcano, and its volcanic soils are part of what critics love about Aglianico del Vulture ([Vintus](https://vintus.com/?p=31844)).

Sources:
- [Vintus, Paternoster in Jancis Robinson's review](https://vintus.com/?p=31844)
- [Wikipedia, Aglianico del Vulture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aglianico_del_Vulture)
